title: Write up a ward falls audit with Vancouver references
person: A ward sister writing up a six-month falls audit for the hospital's nursing quality committee.
review: The report gives 14 falls before the move and 23 after, 9 of the 23 between 22:00 and 06:00, and cites the five sources of the notes as [1] to [5] in order of first mention, the Ashdown Valley policy as a group author, the Lindqvist-Obi article with its first six authors then et al., and the audit-tools web page with its date of citation, 2026 Oct 2.
revised_review: Every in-text number is a superscript, the Pemberton-Ruiz 2023 article is cited in the Method and numbered where it is first cited, the later numbers move up by one in the text and the list, and nothing else changed.
source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; the authors, journals, organisations, DOIs (Crossref test prefix 10.5555) and web addresses (example.org) are invented, and no real study is presented as genuine.
stage_policy: Separate first and revision directories; reveal revision only after first output is frozen.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
Sources are numbered in the order the text first cites them.
The list runs 1 to n in number order, one entry per number.
Every entry is cited and every cited number is listed.
A source cited again keeps its first number and is listed once.
Authors as Surname and initials without full stops, six then et al.
Abbreviated journal titles carry no full stops.
Online sources give [Internet], the date cited and Available from: with the URL.
14 falls before the move, 23 after, 9 of the 23 at night, as in the notes.
No issue, page range or DOI is added for a source the notes give without one.
The trust's falls policy is listed under Ashdown Valley Hospitals Trust as author.
Superscript numbers throughout, the new source numbered where first cited and the rest renumbered; nothing else changed.
